The question asks for some finite dimension and finite distortion; it does not prescribe uniform bounds on either across all such spaces. AimPL, Problem 2.4 Assouad’s theorem with dimension independent of the snowflaking

Background

This question is also known as the Lang–Plaut problem. Its significance is that doubling controls the number of smaller balls needed to cover a ball, while Hilbert embeddability supplies a different, global constraint on distances. Neither condition alone gives the desired conclusion: doubling spaces need not embed bi-Lipschitzly into finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and the problem asks whether the two conditions together suffice. Assouad’s theorem with dimension independent of the snowflaking

Assouad’s theorem gives a nearby but weaker conclusion: for a doubling space and each snowflaking parameter in the stated range, the snowflaked metric embeds bi-Lipschitzly into finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The dimension and distortion in that result may depend on the parameter. Since snowflaking changes the metric, this does not itself answer whether the original metric embeds. The Lang–Plaut formulation recasts the question quantitatively: for each doubling constant, can one bound both the Euclidean dimension and distortion for all doubling subsets of Hilbert space with that constant? OPEN · PROGRESS REPORTED

The problem remains open: a reader submission claims a conditional counterexample, but no independent source verifies it.

The Lang–Plaut problem asks whether every doubling metric space that embeds bi-Lipschitzly into a Hilbert space also embeds bi-Lipschitzly into some finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The question is attributed to Lang and Plaut; the AIM page records it as open.

KNOWN RESULTS

Assouad’s theorem gives finite-dimensional Euclidean embeddings after snowflaking a doubling metric, but not for the original metric.

COMMUNITY SUBMISSION (UNVERIFIED), OCTOBER 25, 2026

A submitted argument claims that a construction in every infinite-dimensional Banach space yields a compact, rectifiable, doubling curve with no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space. Applied to a Hilbert space, it would give a negative answer, but the submission makes this conditional on an upstream nonembedding theorem and supplies no independent verification.

Current status (as of October 2026): The Lang–Plaut problem remains open in the independently retrieved literature; the October 25, 2026 community submission claims conditional progress, but that claim is unverified.
